name: Smart and forthcoming (80K wk1 individual)
notes: Strong student who answers the current question and pre answers the next one. Tests NO REDUNDANT RE-ASK: the bot must advance rather than re asking what was already covered, and must not compliment the quality of the answer.
turns: the biggest one for me was that rules are not just constraints, they are the thing generating the behavior. we read the piece about play being what happens in the space rules leave open and that reframed the whole thing for me
it stood out because i used to think of rules as the boring admin part and the theme was the creative part. now it seems backwards. the rules are where the design actually lives

i made a small trading game with my housemates where you swap chores. i also played the sample game twice, once straight and once with one rule removed, because i wanted to see what the rule was doing

removing the trade limit broke it completely. everyone dumped everything on one person in about two minutes and it stopped being a game. so the limit was not a restriction, it was the thing making the choice interesting
no i think ive covered it. going in i assumed good games came from good ideas

what surprised me was how fast a small rule change killed the whole thing. im still uncertain about how you tell the difference between a rule that is too tight and one that is doing necessary work, without just testing everything
